hypotheses.mechanism: Slide valve (SV-SPENT or SV-REGEN) fails to regulate catalyst flow between RISER and REGENERATOR at 700 °C; last overhauled 6 years ago. Loss of catalyst circulation causes reactor catalyst starvation and regenerator coke accumulation, driving temperature and pressure excursions in both reactors.
hypotheses.consequence: Uncontrolled temperature rise in RISER (coking, tube damage) and REGENERATOR (overpressure, flue gas oxygen breakthrough to EXPANDER/CO-BOILER), potential relief valve discharge to flare, equipment damage in reactor structure.
hypotheses.reason: Both slide valves are 6 years past overhaul per plant notes; they are the sole flow control for 700 °C catalyst circulation between the two reactors. No redundant valve or independent safeguard cited.

hypotheses.mechanism: Main air blower (MAIN-AIR-BLOWER) trips or control valve fails closed, cutting combustion air to REGENERATOR at 2 bar g, 700 °C with coke inventory on catalyst.
hypotheses.consequence: Incomplete coke combustion, afterburn in EXPANDER/CO-BOILER, possible explosion in flue gas path, hot flue gas release to stack area, regenerator overpressure relieved to flare.
hypotheses.reason: Single air blower supplies all combustion air; regenerator operates at 2 bar g with coke on catalyst. SG-E-O2-ANALYSER only indicates, no automatic air backup cited.

hypotheses.mechanism: Catalyst withdrawal line (L-CATALYST-WITHDRAWAL) from REGENERATOR to SPENT-CATALYST-HOPPER leaks or ruptures during withdrawal, releasing 700 °C catalyst and coke to atmosphere.
hypotheses.consequence: High-temperature solids jet impinges on nearby equipment and personnel access areas; potential ignition of hydrocarbon vapours in vicinity; emergency shutdown complicated by catalyst loss.
hypotheses.reason: Line carries 700 °C catalyst during shutdown step P-E-SHUTDOWN-3; no line instrumentation or isolation valves shown in plant record; piping leak cause C20 applies.

hypotheses.mechanism: Major HF acid release from alkylation unit (LOC-E-ALKY, 300 m) due to external fire (C22) or lightning (C26); dense HF vapour cloud drifts to this unit.
hypotheses.consequence: HF vapour reaches reactor structure, control room (120 m), gas plant; severe personnel injury, corrosion damage to hot equipment, potential escalation of local leaks.
hypotheses.reason: HF acid (EPA groups 1, 15) is highly toxic and volatile; 300 m is within dense-gas travel distance; no HF-specific detection or water curtain cited for this unit.

hypotheses.mechanism: Catastrophic failure of an asphalt storage tank (TK-ASPHALT-1 or TK-ASPHALT-2) at 150 °C, 60 m from reactor structure; hot asphalt pool fire impinges on reactor, standpipes, slide valves.
hypotheses.consequence: Pool fire radiates to reactor structure, damages standpipes and slide valves, may cause catalyst circulation loss (hazard 1) and feed line failure; escalates to multi-unit fire.
hypotheses.reason: Two atmospheric tanks at 150 °C only 60 m from reactor structure per LOC-E-ASPHALT; cause C21 (atmospheric tank leaks) applies; fixed fire monitors (SG-E-FIRE-MONITORS) noted but no foam or distance-based protection cited.

hypotheses.mechanism: Operator error during shutdown: slide valves SV-SPENT and SV-REGEN closed too early (before catalyst inventory minimum) or too late, or one left open, per P-E-SHUTDOWN-4.

hypotheses.reason: Shutdown step P-E-SHUTDOWN-4 explicitly requires closing both slide valves as inventory reaches minimum; operator error causes C16 and C17 apply; no valve position interlock cited.

hypotheses.mechanism: Wet gas compressor (WET-GAS-COMPRESSOR) trips during normal operation; cracked vapours back up in MAIN-FRACTIONATOR, pressure rises, relief valves lift to flare.
hypotheses.consequence: Hydrocarbon vapour release to flare via relief valves (SG-E-RELIEF); potential flare overload, thermal radiation to nearby equipment; reactor pressure control upset.
hypotheses.reason: Single compressor handles all cracked vapours; no spare or recycle line shown; compressor trip cause C05 applies; relief to flare is only overpressure path cited.

chains.description: SV-REGEN failing open floods riser with regenerated catalyst while SV-SPENT failing closed traps spent catalyst; blocked vapor outlet L9 prevents pressure relief, causing runaway overheating and overpressure rupture.
chains.reason: L1 raises catalyst/oil ratio and reaction rate; L70 accumulates catalyst and coke; L9 removes the only vapor exit path. All three independently disable riser pressure/temperature control.
flags: possibly more than two independent failures
chains.severity_reason: Runaway overheating and overpressure rupture of the riser vessel releases cracked vapours and catalyst on site; significant release with potential for single fatality or serious injuries to nearby operators.

chains.description: Blower trip drops air header pressure; a leak between the air line and cracked vapour line lets hydrocarbon vapours back-flow into the air system, forming a flammable mixture that can ignite.
chains.reason: L2 creates the pressure reversal; L117 provides the cross-connection path. Neither alone guarantees air/hydrocarbon mixing at ignition concentrations.
chains.severity_reason: Flammable mixture forms in the air header piping and ignites, releasing heat and toxic gases; likely causes lost-time injuries and requires on-site emergency response.

chains.description: Over-speed blower forces excess combustion air into the regenerator while a mispositioned valve leaves spent catalyst in the vessel, greatly increasing coke burn rate and pressure beyond design.
chains.reason: L11 raises oxygen supply and pressure; L26 raises reactive catalyst inventory. Together they drive combustion rate and pressure synergistically.
chains.severity_reason: Excess air and retained catalyst cause runaway coke combustion and overpressure rupture of the regenerator; significant on-site release of flue gas, catalyst and hot coke with potential for serious injuries.

chains.description: A closed manual valve on the feed outlet stops catalyst circulation; closing the slide valves early traps the remaining catalyst in the riser and regenerator with heat still applied, causing severe overheating and overpressure.
chains.reason: L16 eliminates feed-driven catalyst flow; L77 isolates the catalyst inventory. Heat sources remain active, so temperature and pressure rise uncontrollably.
chains.severity_reason: Trapped catalyst in both riser and regenerator with continued heat input causes severe overheating and overpressure; dual vessel rupture releases large inventory of hot catalyst and vapours on site.

chains.description: An external fire heats the feed line, vaporizing HGO and raising pressure; a simultaneous blockage in the same line prevents pressure relief, leading to pipe rupture and HGO release.
chains.reason: L17 adds thermal pressure; L59 removes the hydraulic relief path. The combination exceeds design pressure faster than either alone.
chains.severity_reason: External fire plus blockage ruptures the feed pipe, releasing heavy gas oil (HGO) on site; pool fire risk requires on-site response, likely lost-time injuries.

chains.description: Torch oil introduced into the regenerator creates localized hot spots; excess air from an over-speed blower intensifies combustion, risking runaway temperature and overpressure.
chains.reason: L24 adds a liquid hydrocarbon fuel; L11 adds excess oxidant and pressure. The fire triangle (fuel, oxygen, heat) is completed more severely.
chains.severity_reason: Torch oil creates hot spots and excess air intensifies combustion, leading to runaway temperature and overpressure rupture of the regenerator; significant on-site release.

chains.description: A valve left in the wrong position connects the air header to a hydrocarbon gas line; when the main air blower trips, the pressure drop pulls hydrocarbon vapour into the air system, forming a flammable mixture.
chains.reason: L29 creates the physical connection; L2 creates the pressure differential that drives mixing. Neither alone causes the cross-flow.
chains.severity_reason: C1–C4 gases back-flow into air header on blower trip, forming flammable mixture that ignites in piping; release of heat and toxic gases requires on-site response, likely lost-time injuries.

chains.description: Feed is reduced before steam dilution is established, causing localized overheating and coke buildup in the riser; a blocked vapor outlet prevents pressure relief, leading to overpressure and potential rupture.
chains.reason: L43 initiates thermal degradation; L9 removes the pressure safety valve. Coke buildup from L43 also worsens any blockage.
chains.severity_reason: Early feed reduction causes coke buildup and overheating; blocked vapour outlet prevents relief, leading to riser overpressure rupture with significant release of cracked vapours and catalyst on site.

chains.description: A vehicle impact breaches an asphalt tank; water ingress through a faulty seal generates steam and overpressure, causing catastrophic tank failure and massive hot asphalt release.
chains.reason: L53 creates the initial breach; L103 adds internal pressure that enlarges the breach and ejects contents violently. Mechanical and pressure failures combine.
chains.severity_reason: Vehicle impact breaches tank; water ingress generates steam overpressure causing catastrophic tank failure and massive hot asphalt release 60 m from reactor; multiple on-site fatalities possible.

chains.description: Isolation and blinding for maintenance is performed while catalyst withdrawal is incomplete; the regenerator still holds active catalyst and a hot coke bed. Closing the air block valve cuts off cooling combustion air, leaving the hot inventory isolated with no heat removal.
chains.reason: L79 traps hot catalyst/coke in a confined volume; L80 removes the designed cooling flow. Temperature and pressure can rise until vessel failure.
chains.severity_reason: Isolation during incomplete catalyst withdrawal cuts cooling air to regenerator with hot coke bed; temperature excursion risks catalyst damage and potential release, requiring on-site response.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-high pressure trip on S-RISER (PSHH-RISER) that opens a dedicated pressure relief valve (PRV-RISER) to flare, independent of vapor outlet L9.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for the combined overpressure scenario; this adds an independent engineered layer to mitigate rupture risk when L9 is blocked and catalyst valves fail.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high flow trip on the regenerated catalyst line (FSHH-REGEN) that closes a dedicated block valve (XV-REGEN) upstream of SV-REGEN, using a separate flow sensor.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for SV-REGEN failing open; this removes the cause by an independent engineered layer that stops excess catalyst flow before overheating occurs.

recommendations.action: Install a low pressure trip on the air header (PSL-AIR) that closes an isolation valve (XV-AIR) to prevent hydrocarbon backflow when MAIN-AIR-BLOWER trips, using an independent pressure sensor.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for blower trip leading to flammable mixture; this adds an independent engineered layer that isolates the air system before vapour ingress occurs.

recommendations.action: Add an independent low flow trip on WET-GAS-COMPRESSOR discharge (FSL-WGC-DISCH) that opens a hot gas bypass valve (XV-WGC-BP) to maintain downstream pressure, using a separate flow sensor.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for compressor trip causing low flow; this adds an independent engineered layer that sustains gas plant pressure and avoids process upset or flaring.

recommendations.action: Revise procedure P-E-SHUTDOWN-1 to require confirmed steam dilution flow (via FI-STEAM) before reducing feed, and add a hardware interlock (IL-SD-RISER) that blocks feed reduction valve (SV-FEED) until steam flow exceeds setpoint.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for early feed reduction during shutdown; this removes the procedural cause and adds an independent engineered interlock to prevent overheating and overpressure when vapor outlet is blocked.

recommendations.action: Install a differential pressure transmitter across L-VAPOURS with a high-dP alarm and automatic trip to close the riser feed valve on sustained high differential pressure indicating blockage.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for vapor outlet blockage. This engineered layer detects the cause (fouling/debris in L-VAPOURS) directly and acts before pressure exceeds design, preferred over relief-only or procedural responses.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high-temperature trip on the regenerator that closes the torch oil supply valve and trips the combustion air blower on temperature exceeding the safe operating envelope.
recommendations.reason: No layers guard against combined torch oil ingress and excess air. An independent trip on temperature (not shared with blower speed control) removes both fuel and oxidant simultaneously, addressing the runaway combustion root cause.

recommendations.action: Install a blower speed governor with independent overspeed trip that closes the combustion air supply valve, and add a valve position interlock preventing spent catalyst retention when the regenerator is in combustion mode.
recommendations.reason: No layers address over-speed blower or mispositioned valve. The governor removes the excess air cause; the interlock prevents the spent catalyst condition. Both are engineered, independent of the basic process control system.

recommendations.action: Install a high-pressure trip on the CO-boiler that closes the expander discharge valve and opens the CO-boiler vent to flare on pressure exceeding design, independent of the downstream L-FLUE-3 condition.
recommendations.reason: No layers protect against L-FLUE-3 blockage backpressure. This trip acts on the CO-boiler pressure directly, isolating the boiler from the expander and relieving to flare, preferred over relying on downstream relief or operator response to a blocked flue.

recommendations.action: Install a key-locked valve or dual-solenoid valve with position verification on the air header/hydrocarbon gas line connection, interlocked to prevent opening unless the main air blower is confirmed running.
recommendations.reason: No layers prevent valve mispositioning that creates the cross-connection. A hardware interlock removing the human error cause is preferred over alarms or procedures; it ensures the connection cannot be made when blower trip would draw hydrocarbon vapour into the air system.

recommendations.action: Install a check valve on the air header line at the cracked vapour line tie-in point (C05/C20) to prevent hydrocarbon backflow during blower trip.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist; a check valve directly prevents the backflow cause by engineered hardware rather than relying on procedures or alarms.

recommendations.action: Install a fire water spray system on the S-RISER vessel and associated piping (C22) to mitigate external fire heat input.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist; an engineered fire protection system directly addresses the external fire hazard rather than procedural controls.

recommendations.action: Add a keyed interlock on the catalyst handling valves that requires completion of P-E-SHUTDOWN-3 steps before allowing catalyst exposure to atmosphere.
recommendations.reason: Operator error skipping procedure steps has no engineered barrier; a permissive interlock removes reliance on procedural compliance.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high catalyst flow trip on the regenerator outlet (C01) that closes a dedicated isolation valve on flow above setpoint, independent of SV-REGEN.
recommendations.reason: SV-REGEN fail-open has no independent protection; a separate flow trip with its own valve adds an engineered layer.

recommendations.action: Add a permissive interlock on the slide valves associated with S-L-FEED and S-RISER/S-REGENERATOR that prevents closure until the feed outlet manual valve is confirmed open and heating is isolated, enforcing P-E-SHUTDOWN-7 sequence.
